Fix: honour `opt.visibleWhen` in SchemaForm's select-option mapping through the same `evaluatePredicate` path the node-level predicates use, with a pin per consuming control; if honouring it surfaces a semantic the ADR does not define (e.g. all options filtered out), stop and report the fork.

## Claimed + dispatched — `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat

PM session `session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`, branch `claude/issue-6247-option-visiblewhen-metadata-admin`.
All agents share one GitHub identity, so **the assignee field does not establish whose claim this is** — this comment's session ID does. No earlier claim comment exists on this card.

### 裁决 (binding)

**Honour `opt.visibleWhen` in `SchemaForm`'s select-option mapping, through the same `evaluatePredicate` path the node-level predicates already use.** `SelectOptionSchema.visibleWhen` (ADR-0068 / #2284) parses clean on metadata forms and is silently ignored here — accepted, stored, shipped, and inert. That is the declared≠enforced class.

⛔ **Do not add a second evaluator.** Route through the existing path. A local predicate check bolted onto the option mapping would be a new dialect, and this repo has already paid for that once: #5926's gap 2 records `page:tabs` running its **own** `ExpressionEvaluator` whose `data` root means the **opposite** of the node-level gate's — *same key, opposite meanings*. ⚠️ Do not create a third.

**A pin per consuming control** — triage is explicit. Enumerate which controls consume select options and pin each by name.

### ⛔ Fork clause — binding

**If honouring the key surfaces a semantic ADR-0068 does not define — the obvious one being *all options filtered out* — stop and report.** Do not invent the answer. Other candidates worth checking while you are there: what happens to a currently-**selected** value whose option becomes hidden, and whether a hidden option is merely unlisted or actually unselectable. If the ADR is silent on any of those and your change would have to pick, that is a fork, not an implementation detail.

### PM机制假设 (verify — each can be wrong)

1. `SelectOptionSchema.visibleWhen` is genuinely declared and genuinely parses clean today. **Measure it** against the installed `@objectstack/spec` — and ⚠️ **carry a control**: a key you expect **refused** must actually be refused, or you are measuring a passthrough schema rather than a declared key. (`BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()` with an index signature in this repo, and a dev tonight predicted a TS error on an undeclared key and was **wrong** for exactly that reason.)
2. The node-level predicates in this renderer really do go through a shared `evaluatePredicate`, and it is reachable from the option mapping with the scope it needs. ⚠️ **This is the assumption most likely to break the card.** #6110's dev found tonight that `/forms/:name` had **no predicate scope published above it at all** — `ExpressionProvider` was mounted only over other subtrees — so binding the call sites alone would have read `{}` forever and **shipped inert while the pins went green**. **Trace the scope from where it is published to where you would consume it**, and confirm a provider actually sits above this renderer. If it does not, that is the real card and it is bigger than the option mapping.
3. Confirm the predicate's fail direction here (open or closed) before writing a pin — it decides which assertion can distinguish the two worlds.

### Standing verification rules (non-negotiable)

Predict direction before running. Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and** separately the removed text. Print the landing site. Assert anchor uniqueness bounded to the right span. Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command; confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards (a trap that *fires* is not a trap that *restored* — one fired and failed on a repo-relative pathspec tonight, leaving a dirty tree that read as clean). Derive the gate set by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**. A cached turbo green is not a measurement — use `--force`. Commit before you ablate.

⚠️ **Trap ① — if the predicate fails OPEN, "the option is shown" distinguishes nothing.** It is the outcome of predicate-true, predicate-never-arrived **and** predicate-faulted. Your pin must assert an option is **ABSENT** on a predicate that evaluates false, proven **red before the fix**, with a shown-when-true case only as the control.

⚠️ **Trap ② — a structural pin is not enough.** "The mapping calls `evaluatePredicate`" is satisfiable by a call that receives an empty scope and resolves nothing (see assumption 2). **Pin the rendered option list**, not the call.

⚠️ **Trap ③ (repo-specific false green)**: `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec vitest` and `cd packages/x && pnpm exec vitest` hit a guard (objectui#3378). Behaviour differs by invocation form — one dev saw it **refuse loudly** (`ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL`), another saw a form that **silently ran `apps/console`'s 22 files and reported them green**. **Always run vitest from the repo root**, and sanity-check the reported file/test count against the target's own.

⚠️ **Trap ④ — `tsc` and `vitest` resolve workspace deps DIFFERENTLY**, measured tonight: `vitest.config.mts` aliases `@object-ui/*` to `src/`, while `tsc` resolves through **`dist`** (no tsconfig path mapping). So a type-check red can be **unbuilt siblings**, a **real error in your own diff**, or both at once — a dev tonight got 15 errors that were 14 noise + 1 real, and reading it as either "all noise" or "I broke it" would have been wrong. Build the closure, then re-read.

### Changeset

Required — a **behaviour change**: previously-inert authored metadata starts hiding options. State it in words. ⛔ Never `major`.

### Collision bounds

Four sibling agents are live: **#6176** (`packages/plugin-form` `ObjectForm.tsx`/`MasterDetailForm.tsx`), **#6167** (`examples/schema-catalog/**` + `apps/site/**`), **#5935** (⚠️ **wide** — `packages/components`, `packages/plugin-list`, `packages/plugin-detail`, lucide gate script), **#6165** (`HomeRail` + two sibling consumers).

⚠️ **#5935 is the one to watch** — if `SchemaForm` lives in `packages/components`, you may be in the same package. **Different files is fine; same file is not.** Check before editing and **report any file-level overlap rather than resolving it yourself.** ⛔ Do not edit under `packages/plugin-form/src/`.

⛔ Leave the PR **draft**. Do not mark ready, do not enqueue, do not enable auto-merge — the PM lands it.

The dev confirmed the premise in full, then stopped exactly where the dispatch told it to. **No PR was opened** — deliberately, and the reasoning is right: a `Fixes #6247` on a card returning to the decision box would silently close it.

⛔ **None of the three forks is mine to rule.** One is a dialect decision, one changes a control's identity, one would delete authored metadata during render. I am recording them, not answering them.

### ✅ What was confirmed first (so nobody re-derives it)

- **The key is genuinely declared**, with a working control: `SelectOptionSchema` is `z.core.$strict`, so `bogusKeyNobodyDeclared` and `disabled` are **refused** with `unrecognized_keys`. Not a passthrough artefact.
- ⭐ **#6110's failure mode does NOT apply here.** I flagged it as the likeliest card-killer; the dev checked and scope **is** reachable — metadata-admin renders under `ExpressionProvider` (`app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx:925`) and the draft is already threaded to every consuming control as `formData`. But `SchemaForm`'s `evaluatePredicate` builds `{ data: draft }` **locally and consumes neither**. That distinction is what turns this from a plumbing fix into a dialect question.
- **Exactly three controls** consume `fieldSpec.options`, none reads `visibleWhen`: the builtin Select (`SchemaForm.tsx:1666-1681`), `MultiSelectWidget` (`widgets.tsx:1128`), and `colorPaletteOptions` → `ColorSwatchGroupWidget` (`widgets.tsx:2183`).
- **Fail direction is OPEN**, measured.
- ✅ **One of my fork questions was NOT a fork and was correctly answered from the spec instead of escalated**: a hidden option is **unlisted**, never shown-unselectable — `SelectOptionSchema`'s docblock says *"offered or withheld"* and there is deliberately no `disabled`. Right instinct: escalate what is undefined, answer what is defined.

### ⚠️ FORK A — honouring the key would make the ADR's own headline use case fail OPEN

metadata-admin binds **one** root: `data` (the draft). ADR-0068 defines this key's canonical use as **identity gating** (`'admin' in current_user.positions`), and the sibling runtime surface uses `record.*`.

**Measured: both fail OPEN here regardless of value.** So honouring `visibleWhen` on this surface would make `data.*` predicates work while the two spellings the ADR actually defines it for silently no-op **in the permissive direction — an option gated to admins shown to everyone.**

That is precisely what `predicate-scope-parity-6010.test.tsx` exists to prevent (*"ONE authored `visibleWhen` text, every binding surface, one verdict"*), arriving on a **fourth** surface with its own evaluator.

⚠️ And binding `current_user` is not a clean fix: `ExpressionProvider`'s scope **also carries a `data` key**, meaning the provider's data scope — **not** the draft. Adopting it head-on collides with metadata-admin's `data` = draft. **That is #5926 gap 2's *"same key, opposite meanings"* exactly**, and picking is a dialect decision.

Dev's recommendation: **A2** (bind `current_user` + ADR-0068 aliases alongside `data`, keeping `data` = draft, not adopting the provider's conflicting `data`), plus A1's **loud dev diagnostic** for unresolved roots (`predicate.ts` already has warn-once machinery) — but explicitly **as a maintainer ruling only**, because A1 alone makes the key's headline use case a silent fail-open. I agree with the refusal to choose.

### ⚠️ FORK B — an emptied option list degrades to FREE TEXT, which is the opposite of a narrowing
